extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in aviation safety, corporate accountability, and current events
extracted.subtask_short: timeline news article on Boeing 737 Max
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological timeline-style news article documenting incidents, investigations, corporate actions, and consequences related to the Boeing 737 Max and broader Boeing safety issues. It compiles dates, factual details, quotes, and sources to explain how the situation evolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological timeline structure with explicit dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Present events in chronological order with clear date markers (e.g., 'March 2017', 'October 2018') so readers can follow how incidents and responses unfolded over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use month/year headings and place individual incidents under the appropriate date; connect earlier events to later developments to show continuity and causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite official certifications and regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report certification dates and actions by regulators (e.g., 'FAA certifies Boeing’s 737 Max 8', 'regulators ground the fleet', 'agency clears the Max 8 fleet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include which agency acted, the timing, and whether an action was a grounding, audit, clearance, or new inspection procedure; link to or name primary documents (FAA orders, NTSB preliminary reports, Congressional reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain technical causes and systems (e.g., MCAS, sensors, angle of attack)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe technical contributors to incidents (for example, MCAS activation caused by erroneous sensor data and the role of 'angle of attack' sensors) and how pilots attempted to override systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough technical detail for readers to understand the mechanism of failure (what MCAS did, required pilot actions to retake control) without excessive jargon; when possible, use investigator findings to support the explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document casualty counts and human impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Report fatalities, injuries, and the human toll of accidents (e.g., 'killing 189', 'killing 157', survivor accounts), and include effects on victims' families (lawsuits, demands for prosecution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise numbers from official investigations and note ongoing legal or emotional consequences (class-action suits, victim families pressuring DOJ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record corporate actions, leadership changes, and internal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe corporate responses such as executive removals, CEO statements, internal messages (e.g., concealing MCAS from test pilots, 'I basically lied to the regulators'), and reorganizations (new VP of Quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates and context for personnel moves, summarize relevant internal communications revealed by reporting, and note how those actions relate to accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record whistleblower testimony and allegations about workplace culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Include whistleblower accounts alleging prioritization of profits over safety, 'unstable' production environments, retaliation, and claims of 'dangerous lack of regard for safety.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote whistleblowers when possible, note union complaints (e.g., SPEEA), and document any official hearings or Congressional testimony that include these claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document investigations, audits, and their findings (FAA, NTSB, DOJ, FBI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the existence and outcomes (preliminary or final) of official investigations and audits, including findings like 'dozens of problems', missing bolts, failure to provide evidence of approval for design changes, or ongoing criminal probes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which agencies opened investigations, summarize key findings (e.g., missing bolts on a door plug), and report any resulting enforcement steps or deadlines (FAA 90-day deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover legal and financial consequences (suits, fines, deferred prosecutions, settlements)
rubrics_metrics.description: List legal actions and monetary consequences such as class-action suits, shareholder lawsuits for misleading investors, SEC fines, the $2.5 billion deferred prosecution agreement, compensation payments, and company financial losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide amounts, legal characterizations (deferred prosecution, criminal charge, acquittal), and the relationship between incidents and financial impacts (lost revenue, compensation to airlines, victims, or customers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include supplier and manufacturing quality-control issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe problems at parts suppliers (e.g., Spirit AeroSystems) and on the manufacturing floor, such as 'loose hardware', 'excessive defects', missing bolts, and alleged falsified or missing work records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute findings to inspections, audits, or whistleblowers and note how supplier issues contributed to the incident and subsequent inspections or litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect individual incidents to broader patterns or systemic concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how discrete events (crashes, door blowouts, landing gear failures on other models) may indicate systemic safety or cultural problems across the company rather than isolated anomalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include incidents involving other Boeing models and cite reporting or expert panels that identify patterns (international safety panel blaming Boeing and FAA, multiple whistleblower accounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sourced quotes and link to reporting and original documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Support assertions with quotes from company statements, whistleblowers, regulators, and investigative reporting (e.g., quoting 'I literally saw people jumping on the pieces of the airplane to get them to align' or 'absurd' remark from NTSB chair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed hyperlinks or references to named outlets, Congressional reports, NTSB/FAA documents, and direct company statements to allow readers to verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report ongoing status and evolving developments (preliminary reports, audits, and future deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear when findings are preliminary, investigations are ongoing, or decisions are pending (e.g., NTSB 'preliminary report', DOJ decision deadline July 7 on deferred prosecution), and update readers about new developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag provisional findings vs. final conclusions, include deadlines and next steps, and, in timelines, update earlier entries as investigations progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include operational consequences for airlines and passengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Note immediate operational impacts such as emergency landings, groundings, inspection orders, and airline financial impacts (lost revenue, estimated losses for United/Alaska).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify impacts when possible and tie them to specific incidents and regulatory responses (FAA grounding or inspection directives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance technical/legal detail with readability for general audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain complex regulatory, technical, and legal matters in accessible language while preserving accuracy (e.g., explaining MCAS, angle-of-attack, deferred prosecution agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive jargon; provide concise explanations or parenthetical clarifications so non-expert readers understand significance without losing nuance.
